MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 23, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on April 23, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 18, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Liability Claims; Claimants: Donaldson, Orloff and Gray; Agency Claimed Against –
  City of Mission Viejo and; Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph
  (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (3 cases).

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present

City Council Minutes  1  April 23, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received an update on potential
litigation and liability issues. The Council provided direction to staff but no reportable actions
occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim the Month of April 2019 as Community College Awareness Month

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Elliot Stern, President of Saddleback College, and
  Tim Jemal, Trustee of the South Orange County Community College District.

P2. Featured Businesses of the Month

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to Elyse Congelliere of J. Hilburn Partners and Keith
  and Karin Krawiec of Neighborhood Car Care.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Al Arakawa, M.V.: expressed concern with public parking on street sweeping days and asked the
City Council to consider passing a law to allow for enforcement.

Ashley Brunier: M.V.: speaking on behalf of Waste Management, she said they proudly serve
Mission Viejo and invest in the community through participation at city events. Ms. Brunier
invited residents to stop by and say hello at the 4th of July Street Faire, Symphony in the Cities or
the concerts on the green and take a picture with the Waste Management mini truck.

Jeanne Tumanjan, Dana Point: representing the Wounded Warrior Amputee Softball team, she
thanked the City for its support and hosting the softball team games since 2012. She announced
that the team has a new name: “USA Patriots - Amputee Softball Team.”

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  April 23, 2019
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of April 9, 2019, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated March 29, 2019 in the Amount of $994,452.34

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated April 5, 2019 in the Amount of $452,561.34

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Landscape and Irrigation Supplies

  (1) Awarded the bid for landscape and irrigation supplies to SiteOne Landscape Supply for
  the period of July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2021, in the amount of $600,000.00; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to SiteOne Landscape Supply for the period of July
  1, 2019, through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $300,000.00 pending adoption
  of the 2019-2021 budget by City Council.

5.  Annual Routine Landscape Rodent Pest Control – Contract Area 1 and Contract Area 2

  (1) Awarded both Contract Area 1 and 2 for the subject service to Agricultural Pest Control
  Services for the period of July 1, 2019, to June 30, 2021, in an amount of $66,487.60 for
  Area 1 and in an amount of $33,421.76 for area 2; and (2) authorized issuance of purchase
  orders to Agricultural Pest Control Services for the period of July 1, 2019, to June 30, 2020,
  in an amount not to exceed $33,243.80 for Area 1 and in an amount not to exceed $16,710.88
  for Area 2 pending adoption of the 2019-2021 budget by City Council.

6.  Felipe Road & Olympiad Road Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 19837)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $1,667,000 to Hardy & Harper, Inc. for
  the subject project.

7.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2019-2020 Detailing City’s Proposed
  Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds.

  Adopted Resolution 19-06 Approving the City's Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year
  (FY) 2019-2020 Detailing the City’s Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such Plan to the U.S. Department of Housing
  and Urban Development (HUD).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

8.  Consideration of Participating in the Orange County Finance Trust Via Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority Membership

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  3  April 23, 2019
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) find
  that this action is not subject to the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
  Sections 15060(c)(2) and 15060(c)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines because this action will not
  result in a physical change to the environment, directly or indirectly; and (2) adopted
  Resolution 19-07 Relating to Participating in the Orange County Housing Finance Trust Via
  the Execution of the Joint Powers Agreement Which Implements the Trust's Shared Powers
  and Activities.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  FY 2019-2021 Proposed CIP Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Arthur Wensman, M.V. and Penny Young, M.V:. asked that the Sierra Recreation Center
  improvements be moved up on the CIP list.

  Garrett Mitton, President of South Mission Viejo Little League, M.V.: requested additional
  lights at the Youth Athletic Park and committed $10,000 towards the project.

  Chris Welsh, M.V.: thanked staff for the consideration of Craycraft Park improvements and
  said that Mission Viejo Girls Softball wants to be a partner and will put $10,000 towards the
  project.

  Steve Peters, M.V.: stated that he considers the pools and recreation centers a real jewel of
  Mission Viejo and he hopes that the facilities and their pools will be taken care of.

  The following spoke in favor of improvements at the Sierra and Montanoso Recreation
  Centers: Sam Afshar, M.V.; Doug Fleischli, M.V.; Karl Schultz, M.V.; and Sid Schenk, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to get
  started on the Montanoso and Craycraft projects as soon as possible.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to move
  the Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park additional ballfield lights (item 11) to spot number five
  on the wish list (after the Murray Center improvements).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  April 23, 2019
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Raths, to add a shade structure
  to one park per year and add that as item number six on the CIP list.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley
  NOES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to direct
  staff to incorporate, as a policy, the installation of shade structures in to future park
  rehabilitation projects.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Establish General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for 2019-21 Budget Cycle

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt
  Resolution 19-08 Establishing General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for the
  2019-21 Budget Cycle.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11. Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

12. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

City Council Minutes  5  April 23, 2019
 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

13. Ordinance Clean-up to Several Titles of the City’s Municipal Code

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance 19-328 Amending and Updating the City of Mission Viejo’s Municipal Code
  Sections 6.10.010, 6.65.110, 6.65.310, 13.02.025, 13.02.050, 14.03.230, Adding Section
  6.65.325, of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Relating to Waste Management, Water
  Quality, Vertical Improvements, City Recreation Facilities, Urban Runoff and Conforming
  Cannabis Definitions to Current Federal Law.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum drew attention to the CDBG funding item that was approved on the
Consent Calendar earlier in the meeting. She said those are federal funds and Mission Viejo does
really unique things when it comes to helping the homeless. Some of the CDBG monies are used
to help Families Forward, South County Outreach and Stand Up for Kids which are organizations
that help families to get out of their homeless situation in a very caring and compassionate way.
Council Member Bucknum thanked Council Member Kelley for her report on the Transportation
Corridor Agencies. She said she is very passionate about making sure that the City protects its
citizens with a good quality of life and good mobility for economic reasons. She outlined her
attendance at recent events including the Orange County Sheriff Department’s Medal of Valor
ceremony, the Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly, the FINA Diving
Grand Prix at the Marguerite Aquatics Center, Carl Hankey school's International Education
Foundation fundraiser, Bunny Days, and the South Orange County Economic Report at
Saddleback College. She said she was glad that the Mayor honored the college earlier in the
meeting as she appreciates their partnership and everything they do for the community.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated that she too attended the Economic Report event at Saddleback
College and it was nice to see that all five Council Members were there. She was also present at
the Medal of Valor event where two Mission Viejo deputies were honored with awards for saving
City Council Minutes  6  April 23, 2019
 the life of a woman. She reminded residents of upcoming events including National Prescription
Medication Take-Back Day on April 27 from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at city hall and Boots, Beer
and BBQ on Sunday, July 21 at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. Tickets for the latter
are on sale now at the Murray Center or online at mvcommunityfoundation.org. Council Member
Kelley said she attended the Children’s Environmental Fair with more than 700 of the City’s 3rd
graders and she commended staff member Denise Matson for the great job she has done with that
program each year. She further discussed her attendance at the FINA Diving Grand Prix, the Earth
Day planting event at Cordova Park, Bunny Days, and Viejo Elementary’s celebration of Earth
Day at their school garden. Council Member Kelley concluded her comments by sharing an
educational video that was created by the Sheriff’s department to highlight social media dangers
to kids.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs said he was happy to announce that since the last Council Meeting, the
City of Garden Grove has joined Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) and it is going to be a
great addition for the North County experience to fill a gap where one existed previously. He also
noted that OCFA continues to take steps towards the rebuilding of Mission Viejo’s fire station 9.
He announced that he was contacted by a representative of the California Public Utilities
Commission and he had a good conversation with the individual about what's going on with utility
companies’ pricing and liability issues. Council Member Sachs said he wanted to highlight that
the Commissioners will be setting off on a listening tour and he would like for the tour to come to
Mission Viejo in the fall. He also asked staff to look at Community Choice Aggregate (CCA) and
how it might benefit the City of Mission Viejo. He announced that he will be attending a CCA
summit in June and he will report back on that evet. Council Member Sachs said that Assemblyman
Brough’s bill, AB 1273, is really incendiary to Mission Viejo. The City has 150% of its population
traveling through town every morning and that is a burden on the City that it wasn't built to
accommodate. Council Member Sachs said he hasn't seen any response from the Transportation
Corridor Agencies regarding AB 1273 and the legislature needs to hear both sides of the situation.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell discussed his attendee at the FINA Diving Grand Prix. He said it was an
awesome event and he hopes that residents got to watch the live stream if they weren't able to be
there in person. He noted that there was excellent video coverage provided by the City’s own
production team and it was certainly fun to see athletes and coaches from 25 countries represented,
along with all of the officials from FINA and USA Diving. He said the crowd was fired up and the
caliber of diving was phenomenal. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that there was another dive
meet last week and there is a regional championship next weekend. There will also be a number
of great competitions at the Marguerite Aquatics Center over summer as well with the Masters
National Diving and Swimming Championships and the inaugural competition of the brand-new
professional swimming league the first weekend in October. He discussed his attendance at the
City’s Earth Day celebration where he met a sixth-grader who is building bird boxes and he
attended the South Orange County Economic Coalition Economic Report event in partnership with
Saddleback College. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell stated that it was phenomenal and the report is
available on Saddleback College's website so he encouraged residents to download and read it. In
conclusion, he announced that the Olympic Promotion Committee will be meeting tomorrow to
continue planning efforts to expand and bring more sports to Mission Viejo in the future.

City Council Minutes  7  April 23, 2019
 Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths congratulated the Trabuco Hills High Scholl Marching Band for their invitation to
play in the 2020 Macy's Day Parade. Discussing the FINA diving event, he announced that he met
a man from Brazil who said that Mission Viejo’s aquatics facility is the best he has seen in all of
the world. Mayor Raths gave kudos to head Dive coach Michele Mitchell for making the event
happen and he thanked City staff for their great work. He announced that the Rotary Club will
hold its annual Mayor's Prayer Breakfast on May 2 at the Mission Viejo Country Club beginning
at 7:30 a.m. He also noted that he is the Rotary’s president-elect and he looks forward to taking
over in July. Mayor Raths discussed his ride along with the City’s Code Enforcement staff and
stated that he learned a lot about the work they do to keep Mission Viejo homes and home values
up. He announced that he serves on the Southern California Association of Governments
Environmental and Energy Committee and in that role, he took a tour of an electric car company
in Irvine called Ampere Motors. He said he enjoyed driving the cars around and he thanked
Ampere for what they are doing for the environment. In closing, Mayor Raths thanked the
Chamber of Commerce for all that they do in the community.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting in memory of Gregory Locke and the Christians that were
killed on Easter Day in Sri Lanka, to Tuesday, May 14, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 14, 2019

City Council Minutes  8  April 23, 2019
